summary: Verified coloring canvas bug fix. Found a follow-up rendering bug (Svg overlay stuck at default 300x150 with overflow:hidden — strokes drawn over the illustration were captured in the DOM but visually CLIPPED, so the user's original complaint 'cannot color over the images themselves' still reproduced). Applied a minimal one-line fix: added width="100%" height="100%" props to the <Svg> overlay in /app/frontend/app/coloring/[slug].tsx. After the fix, drag gestures across the CENTER of the line-art image now render visible semi-transparent colored strokes across the illustration itself on both /coloring/cross and /coloring/sacred-heart. All regression flows (color-swatch selection, undo, clear, share alert on web, AsyncStorage persistence across reload) pass.
action_items: Fix already applied by testing agent: added width="100%" height="100%" to the <Svg> overlay in /app/frontend/app/coloring/[slug].tsx so react-native-svg's rendered <svg> element stretches to fill its parent instead of defaulting to 300x150 with overflow:hidden (which was clipping strokes drawn over the illustration). Please retain this change.
Consider adding a viewBox and/or preserveAspectRatio if you plan to support device rotation or Android scaling edge cases, but not required for current mobile/web behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: react-native-svg on web does NOT translate CSS position:absolute + top/left/right/bottom:0 (from StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject) into a stretched SVG rectangle — the underlying <svg> element keeps its intrinsic 300x150 size. Always pass explicit width/height props (percent strings or numeric pixels) to <Svg> when it must overlay a container.

AsyncStorage on web (localStorage) persists coloring_progress_<slug>. Since the fix now renders strokes correctly, any strokes saved before the fix (which were previously invisible) will suddenly reappear over the illustration — expected but worth noting.
Minor: Path opacity 0.55 is a fine default, but on very dark line art the semi-transparent stroke may look muted; consider making it 0.6-0.7 or exposing an opacity slider later.
seed_data_creation: None. Cleared localStorage 'coloring_progress_<slug>' between tests to start each drawing session fresh.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The primary bug (draw over the illustration image) is now fully resolved. The root cause was NOT the PanResponder placement — main agent's fix of moving PanResponder onto a top touch layer was correct and needed. But an additional issue was hiding it: react-native-svg's default HTML <svg> intrinsic size (300x150 with overflow:hidden) clipped any stroke drawn below y=150 in the canvas — which happens to be exactly where the illustration sits. Both fixes are now in place: (1) top-layer PanResponder for uniform touch capture, (2) width/height 100% on the <Svg> to render strokes across the full canvas.
rca_of_issue: Reproduction: Before the width/height fix, open /coloring/sacred-heart, pick red, drag horizontally across the center of the heart. DOM inspection showed an SVG <path> element with correct d= 'M 128 291 L ...' but visually nothing appeared over the illustration. Drawing at y<150 (e.g., top margin above the image) DID show strokes. Root cause: the react-native-svg component renders as HTML <svg>. Without width/height props, browsers apply the SVG intrinsic default of 300x150 and SVG's default overflow:hidden clips any content outside. StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject (position:absolute; top/left/right/bottom:0) does not stretch an <svg> element on web because <svg> lays out based on its intrinsic width/height attributes, not its CSS box. Mitigation: pass width="100%" height="100%" as SVG attributes, which react-native-svg forwards, causing the <svg> to inherit the parent container's dimensions.
